parameters.identity: Source: the rigid blue-and-silver rectangular carton printed Cream Cheese, lying broad-face-up on the wooden tabletop. Its printed top and narrow side walls are visible in the current images. Destination: the empty open bowl with a dark exterior, thin yellow-gold rim, and black-and-white floral patterned interior. This is distinct from the nearby white plate with red rings. The selected top corners, landmarks, and textured patch belong to the cream cheese package; k0 through k5 and floor belong to the bowl.

l1: Curved white opening stroke of the capital C beginning the printed word Cheese.
l2: Center of the small pale lettering inside the dark-blue oval emblem beside the Cream Cheese script.

evidence.explanation: The source is the blue-and-silver rectangular cream cheese package, and the destination is the open patterned bowl beside it, not the red-ringed plate. The package has a visible planar printed top and visible narrow side faces meeting the tabletop, supporting the local model of a rigid package resting flat on one support. Its underside is not observed or inferred from a top sample. The bowl has a visible approximately circular inner lip and cavity bottom, with no visible object covering its opening. The selected textured patch is on the package top. No manipulation or placement has yet occurred.

evidence.explanation:
The proposed high_alignment action is locally supported with the gripper open. This is a high lateral alignment, not a descent or a placement. The current pad height is approximately 1.169 m, and the supplied target finger envelope has a lowest height of approximately 1.156 m. The visible carton, bowl, tabletop and intervening objects lie below this high segment; the tall rack and cabinet are lateral to it. No observed external material obstructs this segment. This is local evidence, not a complete later-corridor clearance certificate.

The current and earlier images show the same Cream Cheese carton, printed face up, and the same empty patterned bowl. There is no visible displacement or identity disagreement, and no intervening execution suggesting disturbance of the bowl/support prior. The action-relevant scene is visible across the two cameras; the dark wrist-view foreground is robot geometry, not an external obstacle.

The returned l0-l2 and k0-k5/floor preserve the earlier visible landmark identities. The p0-p3 points are the tracking-patch vertices, not the outer carton corners. Regions return current carton, bowl, nearby support and scene geometry. This approval does not establish finger-lane clearance for a subsequent descent, retention, or task completion; an inner-lip bounding-box gap alone would not establish those.

The proposed source_hover descent with the gripper open is locally supported, not a later grasp or transfer. The same Cream Cheese carton remains broad-face-up beside the patterned bowl. Its printing and boundaries agree with the earlier images and the reported near-identity registration; no target displacement or identity inconsistency is visible. The bowl and support also show no disagreement with the short-horizon prior, and the acknowledged high approach shows no apparent interaction with them.

The visible tabletop in both finger lanes near the selected package end contains no observed obstructing material. The open fingers bracket the package width. The end-biased pad footprint has finite length overlap with the package, consistent with the supplied 0.0135 m side-overlap estimate; it need not be centered. At this hover endpoint, the supplied lowest finger height is about 0.9546 m, above the package top near 0.918 m and above the visible rim consistent with the prior 0.948-0.950 m measurements. These observations and the own geometry support this limited descent. The inner-lip bounding-box gap is only a proxy, not a collision or clearance certificate.

The wrist hides part of the lower-right bowl area in the hand view, but not the package or the relevant local approach lanes; the agent view supplies additional bowl surface coverage. Selected regions provide current source, lane, bowl and support samples. Hidden package undersides and hidden bowl surfaces are not measured. No retention, subsequent contact descent, or complete transfer-corridor clearance is asserted.

The proposed open-gripper grasp descent is locally supported, not a later transfer or placement. The current carton appearance and visible edges agree with the earlier cream cheese package; the supplied registration also supports no meaningful displacement. The wrist view shows exposed tabletop in both projected finger lanes. With the supplied own geometry, the end-biased grasp has approximately 13.5 mm longitudinal pad/side overlap, and the target pad height gives finite vertical overlap with the carton sides. It need not be centered along the carton. The proposed envelope bottoms at approximately 0.9031 m against the approximately 0.9000 m support plane: a small positive model margin, not a clearance certificate.

No observed external material obstructs these local lanes. The visible bowl rim and wall remain consistent with the earlier pose. The preceding approach remained above the bowl rim, with no visible interaction or displacement requiring that short-horizon prior to be discarded. The nearby hidden rim is not freshly measured, and an inner-lip bounding-box gap alone would not establish clearance. Here the visible thin rim/wall profile, earlier bowl geometry, exposed lane support, and separated finger geometry jointly support this limited descent.

Visibility is self_occluded: the robot hides the far carton end and the bowl's right rim. l1 and l2 are obtainable in agentview although hidden in the wrist view. p2, p3, source_top_corner_2, source_top_corner_3, k4, and k5 cannot be reliably remeasured from these current images and are not returned as fresh points. The returned near-corner samples lie just inside the visible top vertices. No retention, completed placement, or global clearance is claimed.

Bracketing is observed locally. Compared with the earlier elevated view, the current agentview shows the actual open fingertips lowered beside opposite sides of the exposed cream cheese carton end. The wrist view also shows both fingers flanking that same end, with visible tabletop gaps between the fingers and carton. No table penetration or neighboring object intrusion is observed in this local bracket. The gripper body obscures the lower contact area and much of the carton; this is robot self-occlusion, not an observed external obstruction. This observation does not establish contact, retention, or task completion.
